summary: Ideas worth discussing once a threshold is crossed. These are proposals, not Work items: nothing here is planned, owned or authorized. When one becomes real, capture it through Capture Discovered Work and set its status to CAPTURED with the new Work ref.

entries.title: Find the commit where a pathway changed
entries.idea: Pick a control and two builds; the lens binary-searches the commits between them in the browser and stops at the first commit where that control's pathway changed, using the same step-level comparison the Changes panel shows.
entries.why: Turns 'when did Dark mode start returning VexMethod.Result?' into one click instead of reading history. The pieces already exist: any-commit projection and comparePathwayRevision.
entries.threshold: After Main and Stable diverge for the first time, so there is real history to search.

entries.title: Compare any two builds
entries.idea: Let the Changes panel take any base, not only Stable: Main against a commit, one commit against another.
entries.why: Stable is the right default, but debugging an older regression needs two arbitrary points.
entries.threshold: Same as meaning-bisect; build it first if bisect waits.

entries.title: Main follows VexLife-Android on its own
entries.idea: When VexLife-Android main moves, run npm run lens:main and open a pull request with the new Main build and its Changes summary. Stable still moves only by promote.
entries.why: Today Main moves when someone remembers. The pointer would then always say where source really is, and the PR body would say what that means in meaning, not files.
entries.threshold: When Victor wants Main to track source without asking, and VexWork decides whether it runs CI.

entries.title: A Screen Lens for VexLife Prod
entries.idea: VexLife Prod's VexUiBlueprint is already explicit Kotlin. Export it into the Screen Lens schema from a test in that repository instead of parsing text, then register Stable and Main builds in the catalog.
entries.why: The projects entry already shows VexLife Prod; this gives it the same four faces and makes Android and Prod comparable side by side.
entries.threshold: When VexLife Prod has an accepted presentation lifecycle to project.

entries.title: VexBoard seen through its own lens
entries.idea: Project the projects entry and the Screen Lens as screens, with their page state (selection, flips, walk, build) as a small SCAE Family, so VexBoard dogfoods the architecture it shows.
entries.why: It is the honest test of the architecture on a web surface, and it is the meta view Victor asked for.
entries.threshold: After the projects entry settles through a round of lived use.

entries.title: Show where projects meet
entries.idea: Link VexLife Prod alignment entries to the Android screens and controls they correspond to, by stable identity, and open both lenses side by side at the matching point.
entries.why: The projects entry lists projects next to each other; this would show how they connect, which is the comparison Victor described.
entries.threshold: Once VexLife Prod has a lens.

entries.title: History for one control
entries.idea: In the inspector, list the builds and commits where the selected control or its pathway changed, each opening the lens at that point.
entries.why: Gives every control a memory, so an AI picking up work sees what moved recently before touching it.
entries.threshold: After meaning-bisect, which provides the search.

entries.title: What actually happened, over what the code says
entries.idea: Overlay a VexLogger export onto a pathway (which steps ran, in what order, how long) and put real screenshots on the Surface face.
entries.why: The lens shows meaning from source; this would show it lived, and make drift between the two visible.
